title: Synthetic editorial renderer fixture
audience: QA engineers configuring their first reusable browser test plan
goal: Save a correctly mapped plan, execute its reviewed scope and interpret the result.
summary: Turn a test suite into a reusable browser execution. Configure the plan, check its coverage, and learn where to inspect the first run.
prerequisites: Access to the intended ContextQA workspace and permission to create plans.
A small test suite containing reviewed, executable cases for a non-production application.
A known environment, test account and sample data appropriate for those cases.
An available browser target and approval for the scope and cost of execution.

sections.title: What you are configuring
paragraphs: A suite groups test cases. A plan adds the execution configuration: which suites run, which browsers or devices they use, and which execution settings apply. Create the suite first; a plan does not create the test cases for you.

This walkthrough uses a Kan suite and a Chromium desktop target. Substitute a small, known suite for your application. The example screenshots were captured from Ship 5 on November 20, 2026. Workspace options may differ.

The example was saved as plan 38, with one suite and seven cases. Creation and configuration were observed directly. The execution instructions below come from the published product guide; this example has not been executed.

sections.title: 1. Name the plan and choose a viewport
paragraphs: Use a name that identifies the application and purpose. A name such as Checkout smoke — staging is easier to recognize in run history than Test plan 1.
The viewport controls the browser dimensions used by the test. Choose the layout your cases are intended to exercise; a desktop screenshot does not establish mobile coverage.
steps: Open Plans → Test Plans, then select New Test Plan.
Enter a Test Plan Name. In this walkthrough, use Documentation walkthrough — Kan smoke.
Optionally add labels and a description explaining the scope and owner.
Review Hide on Dashboard and Send Notification. Keep notifications off for this walkthrough unless recipients are intended to receive run updates.
Select Desktop and Full HD (1920×1080), then select Next.
sections.expected: The wizard advances to Test Machines & Suites Selection.

sections.title: 2. Add the suite you want to run
paragraphs: Choose a suite whose cases you have already reviewed. Selecting a suite defines the scope of a later execution; it is not just a display label.
The picker separates available suites from selected suites. Moving a suite to the right-hand side stages the choice; Add applies it to the wizard.
steps: Select Add Test Suites.
Search by suite name. The example searches for Kan.
Select the checkbox beside the intended suite in Available Test Suites, then use the right-arrow control to move it into Selected Test Suites.
Confirm that only the intended suites are selected, then select Add.
sections.expected: The selected suite appears in the wizard. It still needs a machine or device mapping.

sections.title: 3. Assign a browser to the suite
paragraphs: Adding a suite and choosing a browser are separate actions. Select the suite row first so the wizard knows which suite receives the new configuration.
Use a descriptive configuration name such as Chromium desktop. Additional targets are useful for cross-browser coverage, but start with one target while validating a new plan.
steps: Select the checkbox beside the suite row, then select Add Machine/Device.
Enter Chromium desktop in Name.
Choose ContextQA Lab for Test Lab Type and Web Browser for Select Platform, where these options are available.
Select Chromium in Browser, then select Create in the machine panel.
Confirm that Chromium desktop appears on the suite row, then select Next.
sections.expected: The machine is listed on the left and its name is attached to the suite on the right.

sections.title: 4. Review execution and evidence settings
paragraphs: Start with one parallel execution while you check the plan. Higher parallelism changes resource use and should match both your tests and the account capacity.

The Environments field supplies environment-specific configuration. Review the target and the cases’ own bindings before running; an empty plan-level selection is not proof that a safe staging environment will be used.
Capture Screenshots determines the evidence available after execution. All Steps is useful for documenting a workflow, but review captured pixels before sharing them.
steps: Set Parallel Execution to 1.
Expand Additional Settings. Review Page Load Timeout and Element Timeout against the application’s needs; the observed defaults are 30.
Choose the intended environment if the plan requires one, and verify the selected suite’s case configuration.
Set Capture Screenshots to All Steps when step-by-step evidence is needed. Review any Knowledge Base selection.
Expand Recovery Actions and review the failure behavior. Avoid enabling automatic reruns without considering their execution scope.
Select Create to save the plan.
sections.expected: The Overview page opens for the saved plan.

sections.title: 5. Check the saved configuration
paragraphs: Before the first execution, confirm the plan contains the cases and browser you intended. A suite can exist with no executable cases, so the suite count alone is insufficient.
In this example, Overview shows one suite, seven cases and Chromium. The latest-run fields are blank because the plan has not run. Saving a plan and running it are separate operations.
steps: On Overview, check the suite and test-case totals in the header.
Inspect Suites in plan and verify the browser/device mapping.
Use View Test Cases to check the cases in the selected suite before authorizing execution.
Open Settings if execution settings need to change, or use the header menu → Edit to revisit the wizard.
sections.expected: The saved plan contains the intended cases and targets, with no unexpected suite or browser mapping.

sections.title: 6. Start and monitor the first run
paragraphs: The following execution procedure is documented in the Learning Hub. The saved example has not been run, so the screenshot below shows its initial empty history rather than a successful result.

Run Now executes the saved configuration and may consume execution capacity or incur charges. Confirm the environment, case behavior and run scope first. Do not start a second run merely because the first has not appeared immediately.
steps: Return to the plan header and select Run Now once after the run scope is approved.
Open Runs. During an active execution, use Live execution to inspect running and queued cases.
After execution finishes, open the corresponding run in Run history or Reports.
Inspect the case and step outcomes, together with any available screenshots and recordings.
sections.expected: A completed run has a recorded outcome for the expected cases. Completion alone is not a pass; check failures, skipped cases and missing executions.

sections.title: How to decide whether the run achieved its goal
paragraphs: First check that the result belongs to the intended plan, environment and execution. An older successful run does not validate a newly changed configuration.
Then compare the executed cases with the planned scope. Investigate failed, aborted, skipped or not-executed cases rather than treating a completed status as successful coverage.
Use step-level evidence to explain what happened. A screenshot can show a page state, while the assertion result establishes whether the check passed. Keep these two kinds of evidence distinct.
If the execution is blocked by configuration or infrastructure, correct that issue before using the result to update a successful product walkthrough.

sections.title: When something does not work
paragraphs: Add Machine/Device is disabled: select at least one suite row. The button applies a target to the selected suites.
Next does not advance from suite selection: confirm that a selected suite has a browser or device configuration attached.
The plan shows zero test cases: open the suite and add compatible cases through Manage Test Cases, then check the plan totals again.
The plan is missing from the dashboard: review Hide on Dashboard in the plan settings.
Run Now is disabled: check that the plan has executable cases. If the run is queued, inspect capacity and the active run state rather than starting another execution.
A failure occurs after execution starts: open the failed case and its step evidence. Check environment values, prerequisites and browser configuration before changing the documented procedure.
